polish.title: Clean up my wording
polish.description: A fast model rewrites the structure — punctuation, capitalization, filler words and sentence breaks. Your exact words and their meaning are kept, and the raw text is always saved in your history.
polish.sends_text: While this is on, your finished transcript is sent to the model you pick below; if your speech recognition already runs on this computer, the wording pass stays here too unless you choose a cloud model yourself. Your raw text is always kept in your history, exactly as it was recognized.
polish.precision_description: Goes one step further and also changes WHICH words are used: a vague placeholder becomes the word you actually meant, and padding collapses into the plain verb — "make a decision" becomes "decide". Simple and exact. It will never swap a normal word for a longer one just to sound impressive.
polish.precision_tradeoff: In exchange, one safety check is relaxed: replacing an unusual word is now allowed, so a word the model misheard can be replaced rather than flagged. Your names, your numbers and your dictionary terms stay protected, and the original transcript is always kept. Applies to translated dictation too.
polish.conversation_description: Applies the same clean-up to what you say in an ordinary conversation, not just to dictation — so the transcript view and your session history read as written sentences instead of raw speech.
polish.conversation_latency: It never slows a reply down: the assistant answers your raw words straight away, and the tidied version arrives a moment later. What was actually said is always kept alongside it.

polish.provider_hint: Automatic takes a key you already have and moves to a different provider when one is rate-limited or out of credit. Pin one only if you want a specific account billed.
polish.test_hint: Runs one fixed sample through your setup. Nothing is saved.

slots.title: Capability slots
slots.storage_postgres_hint: Add the PostgreSQL connection string in API Keys before activating this backend.
slots.embedding_desc: Turns text into vectors for semantic search. Changing it re-embeds everything.
slots.distill_desc: Summarizes ingested items in the background. Applies to new work only.
slots.rerank_desc: Re-orders the fused hits; search works without it.
slots.floor_hint: Only applies when Jarvis brings something up on its own - in voice answers or as background for a chat reply. Results graded below this are left out, and Jarvis says it has nothing instead of volunteering a weak match. Searches you type here always show everything. 0 turns the floor off.
slots.reembed_started: The new index is being built in the background — search keeps using the current one until it is ready.
slots.reembed_body: Every model stores meaning in its own coordinate system, so the {0} embedded items have to be measured again with the new one — old and new values cannot be compared. The rebuild runs in the background, and search keeps answering from the current index until the new one is complete. Nothing is deleted meanwhile, so you can switch back at any time.
slots.reembed_progress: Building the new search index: {0} of {1} passages. Search is unaffected.

slots.storage_restart_hint: A storage change takes effect the next time Jarvis starts. Nothing is deleted, and the current store keeps answering until then.
slots.embedding_lock_hint: This slot has no automatic fallback on purpose: the provider and model together define the vector space of your whole memory, so Jarvis never switches it silently.
slots.distill_auto_desc: Uses whichever chat provider you already have a working credential for, and moves on to the next one if it is rate limited or out of credit. The safe default.
slots.rerank_off_desc: Search still works: results keep the order the keyword and semantic legs agreed on. Turn a reranker on for sharper answers to precise questions.
